text: The platform runs as one platform identity in namespace `rwb-recovery` on task queue `rwb-platform`, with the flexible-server backup window and the restore right held by the operations group for the platform administrator; the archive container `rwb-temporal-archive` is write-once for the archive period of the archived history; and the values the legacy story already fixes are kept unchanged: retention 30 days (DL26), archive lead time 7 days, the archive run at 02:00, a retry count of three and a backup window of at least 35 days.
why: The platform is described by its namespace and its work, not by an identity: Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so no read source names the platform login, the provisioning record of task queue `rwb-platform`, the owner of the backup and restore right, the immutability period of the archive container or the approved server and SDK release. The story cannot start its drills or its archive run without a working read, and it may not invent the values, so one assumption row carries the read and the placeholder stays wherever the value is still open (CG-B-PLT-WF-02-E2039-APP-1).
read: Architecture v5 slide 44 and the Ownership Map give the platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 the owner PLT on task queue `rwb-platform` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and slide 24 makes the queue and namespace the platform's unit of isolation; the ACE recovery objectives (NFR-022, NFR-023, DL11) bound the restore and failover drills, so the flexible server keeps automated backups and point-in-time restore inside them; the archive container is write-once for at least the archive period of a history, because a manifest row is only evidence while the file it names cannot change; and the values the legacy story fixes (30 days, 7 days, 02:00, three retries, a 35-day backup window) are configuration and are not re-derived here.
confirm: Platform team with the operations group, before the SIT drills of wave 0: confirm the platform login and its grants, the task queue `rwb-platform` provisioning record, the role that holds the backup window and the restore right, the immutability period of `rwb-temporal-archive`, and the approved Temporal server and SDK release.
impact: If the read is wrong the drills and the archive run are started under the wrong identity or against a server whose backup window does not cover the recovery point objective: the restore drill would then measure a recovery the live server cannot meet, and the archive could write a file whose immutability ends before its manifest row is needed as evidence. The retention, the lead time, the 02:00 cadence and the retry count do not move, because the legacy story fixes them.
